en: Victorious is Piṅgala-nāga, whose intellect was purified through the grace of Śiva, and whose treatise on speech— measured by the syllables ma, ya, ra, sa, ta, ja, bha, na, la, ga— circulates throughout the world.
Know the letter *ma* to be the "heavy-heavy" (*triguru*), accompanied by the "light-initial" (*laghvādi*) and called the letter *ya*;
the letter *ra* is the "light-middle" (*laghumadhya*), while the letter *sa* is bound at the end as a "heavy" (*guru*).

One should know that the letter *ta* at the end is light, while the letter *ja* is light in both [the first and second feet]. Furthermore, the letter *bha* has a heavy syllable at its beginning, whereas the letter *na* here in the Paiṅgala system is entirely light.

A syllable is heavy when followed by a long conjunction of consonants, or likewise when it ends in a vowel or a consonant, or when it ends in a sibilant (ūṣman), or when it is accompanied by an anusvāra; in some cases, even at the end of a line, a syllable is light if it is the final one.
In the beginning, middle, and end, the syllables ya, ra, ta, and na attain lightness;
bha and ja attain heaviness; but ma possesses both heaviness and lightness.

Piṅgala stated at the beginning of his treatise that a pause consists of three stops and a duration of ten syllables for six months, for the purpose of [defining] the class of meters, word-meanings, and suffixes. 1.1.

Glau. 1.14. "The Vasus are eight. 1.15. Metre. 2.1.

Three times for the *ṛc*s. 2.8. He should increase by two each for the *sāman*s. 2.9. By three each for the *ṛc*s. 2.10.
Four each for those of Prajāpati; one each for the remainder. One should abandon that of Asura.
These are the *uṣṇih*, *anuṣṭubh*, *bṛhatī*, *paṅkti*, *triṣṭubh*, and *jagatī*.
(2.14) Three each bear the same names, while one each belongs to Brahmā. (2.15) Prior to the *yajus* formulas, they belong to the Ṛṣis. (2.16)
The quarter-verse. 3.1.
Filled by *iy* and so forth. 3.2.
The Vasus [are the syllables] of the *gāyatrī*. 3.3.
The Ādityas are from the Jagatī; 3.4. The quarters are from the Virāj; 3.5. The Rudras are from the Triṣṭubh; 3.6.
One, two, three, or four feet, as previously stated; 3.7. The first [type] has four feet with [the syllables of] the seasons (six); 3.8.
In some cases, it has three feet with [the syllables of] the sages (seven); 3.9.
That is *pādanicṛt*. 3.10. With six and seven syllables, and eight in the middle, it is *atipādanicṛt*. 3.11. Two groups of nine and a group of six constitute *nāgī*. 3.12.
Vārāhī is the reverse. 3.13.
Increasing by sixes, sevens, and eights. 3.13.
Pratiṣṭhā is the reverse. 3.15.
The third [verse] consists of two pādas in the Jāgata and Gāyatra meters; 3.16.
Three pādas in the Triṣṭubh meter; 3.17.
Two in the Uṣṇih and Gāyatra meters and one in the Jāgata; 3.18.
If the last [syllable] is in the middle of the *kakubh*, it is [the *kakubh*]. 3.19.
The *puroṣṇih* has [the heavy syllable] before; 3.20.
The *paroṣṇih* has [the heavy syllable] after. 3.21.
3.22. [The *anuṣṭubh*] consists of four feet [of eight syllables each] according to the Ṛṣis. 3.23. The *gāyatrī* consists of [three feet of eight syllables each].
3.24. In some cases, it consists of three feet, including two [feet] of twelve syllables (*jagatī*).
In the middle and at the end. (3.25) The Bṛhatī consists of one Jāgata and three Gāyatrīs. (3.26) It is called Pathyā if the third [foot] is the first. (3.27)
The *nyaṅkusāriṇī* is the second [type]. 3.28.
The *skandhogrīvī* belongs to Krauṣṭuki. 3.29.
The *robr̥hatī* belongs to Yāska. 3.30.
At the end [of the sequence], there is a *bṛhatī* above (3.31).
A *bṛhatī* is at the front (3.32). In some cases, there are four groups of nine (3.33).
The Vairāja and Gāyatra [metres] are [thus defined]. 3.34.
A Mahābṛhatī consists of three Jagatī [feet]. 3.35.
The Tāṇḍins call it a Satobṛhatī. 3.36.
The *paṅkti* consists of two *jagatī*s and two *gāyatrī*s.
(3.37) If the first two [feet] are odd-numbered *sataḥ*, it is a *paṅkti*. (3.38) And if they are the reverse, [it is also a *paṅkti*]. (3.39)
Āstārapaṅkti at the end; 3.40.
Prastārapaṅkti at the beginning; 3.41.
Viṣṭārapaṅkti in the middle; 3.42.
The *saṃstārapaṅkti* consists of five [syllables] outside. 3.43. The *akṣarapaṅkti* consists of four groups of five [syllables]. 3.44.
Both [of these] also [occur] rarely. 3.45.
The *padapaṅkti* consists of five [feet]. (3.46) Four, six, and three [syllables]. (3.47) The *pathyā* consists of five *gāyatra* feet. (3.48)
The *jagatī* [consists] of six [syllables per pada]; 3.49.
The *triṣṭubh* is *jyotiṣmatī* with one [additional syllable]; 3.50.
Likewise the *jagatī*; 3.51.
One should offer with the first [verse] while facing eastward;
with the middle [verse], while facing toward the center;
and with the last [verse], while facing upward.
In the first pentad, the *chandaḥ* is the *śaṅkumatī* (3.55).
In the hexad, it is the *kakudmatī* (3.56). That which ends with three feet and has a middle [foot] that is shorter is the *pipīlikamadhyā* (3.57).

The *viparītā* has its middle [foot] as *yavamadhyā*. (3.58) With one syllable less or more, they are *nicṛt* and *bhurij* respectively. (3.59) With two syllables less or more, they are *virāṭ* and *svarāj* respectively. (3.60)
[The rule applies] when there is doubt from the beginning [of the mantra].
(3.61) And also when [the deity] begins with "devatā.
(3.62) Agni, Savitṛ, Soma, Bṛhaspati, Mitra-Varuṇa, Indra, and the Viśvedevas are the deities. (3.63)
The notes are ṣaḍja, ṛṣabha, gāndhāra, madhyama, pañcama, dhaivata, and niṣāda.
(3.64) The colors are white, spotted, tawny, black, blue, red, and fair.
(3.65) The lineages are Āgniveśya, Kāśyapa, Gautama, Āṅgirasa, Bhārgava, Kauśika, and Vāsiṣṭha. (3.66)
The *aticchandas* meters are dark-colored (śyāma). (3.67) The *kṛti* meters have the luster of yellow pigment (*rocanā*). (3.68) For those not mentioned, the colors may be chosen at will. (3.69)
Four hundred is *utkṛti*. 4.1.
One should omit four from each [successive term] starting from *utkṛti*. 4.2.
These are called *kṛti* when they are applied to the *abhisaṃvyāpra* meters. 4.3.
And by their very nature, they are devoid of prefixes.
4.4. The *dhṛti*, *aṣṭi*, *śakvarī*, and *jagatī* [are formed] as follows: 4.5. These same [names] apply to them individually according to the preceding [rules]. 4.6.
The second [verse] is from the second *Atimāna* hymn. 4.7.
Now, the worldly [verses]. 4.8.
And whatever is *ārṣa* (of rishi-origination) following the *ātreṣṭubha*. 4.9.
A quarter is one-fourth part. 4.10. Or [the verse may end] with the completion of the meter. 4.11. *la* is the *samudrā* group. 4.12.
The middle and beginning [gaṇas] are *ga*, *na*, and *la*. (4.13) The vowels and half a vowel constitute half an *āryā*.
(4.14) In this [half], there is no odd *ja* [gaṇa]. (4.15)
The sixth [section]. 4.16. If there are *n* and *l*, it is optional. 4.17. If there are *n* and *l*, the word begins with the second [syllable]. 4.18.
The seventh [note] occurs from the first [note] onwards (4.19);
the fifth [occurs] at the end (4.20);
and the sixth is mobile (4.21).

In the three groups [of gaṇas], the *pāda* is [regular] in the *pathyā* and other [types]; 4.22. The other is *vipulā*. 4.23. In *capalā*, the second and fourth [groups] have *ga* and *ja* in the middle. 4.24.
When the face is foremost, it is *pūrvā*; 4.25. When the hips are foremost, it is *itarā*; 4.26. When both are foremost, it is *mahācapalā*. 4.27.
The *gīti* consists of the first half [of the *udgīti*] plus an equal number of syllables. 4.28.
The *upagīti* consists of the last [half]. 4.29.
The *udgīti* is formed by reversing the order. 4.30.
In the first half [of the verse], there is a Vasu-group Āryāgīti (4.31).
Vaitālīya consists of two vowels in the odd pāda, with *yu*, *ga*, *va*, and *sa* at the end, followed by *la-ga* (4.32).
Gaupacchandasika is [the same as] this. (4.33)

The *āpātalikā* consists of [the sequence] *bhagaug*. (4.34) In the remaining cases, it is not joined with what follows. (4.35) In the odd-numbered [feet], there are six *ca* syllables that are unmixed. (4.36)

With the fifth [note], the eastern style (prācyavṛtti) occurs simultaneously; 4.37. With the third [note] unjoined, the northern style (udīcyavṛtti) occurs; 4.38. By these two together, the simultaneous occurrence (yugapatpravṛttaka) arises; 4.39.
Ayukcāruhāsinī || 4.40 || Yugaparāntikā || 4.41 || Gantā has twice eight (sixteen) mātrās; the ninth is equal to the kalā. || 4.42 ||
And the *vānavāsikā* has twelve [syllables]; 4.43.
The *viśloka* has five and eight [syllables]; 4.44. And the *citrā* has nine; 4.45.
Upacitrā consists of two *parayukta* [gaṇas]. 4.46.
By these [rules], Pādākulaka is formed. 4.47.
Gītyāryā is characterized by *la* [laghu] at the end. 4.48.
The *śikhā* [meter] consists of half [the preceding meter] reversed. 4.49.
If *la* is first, it is *jyotiḥ*. 4.50. If *ga* is first, it is *saumyā*. 4.51.
There is one *cūlikā* at the end of twenty-nine and thirty-one [verses]. 4.52. It is equal to the *lāṅgala* by way of its syllables. 4.53. [This is] the meter (*vṛtta*). 5.1.
Even, half-even, and uneven.
5.2. First, that which is made [repeatedly] is even; half-even and uneven are likewise. 5.3. Less than the heap. 5.4.
The *gliti* is the *samānī*. 5.5. The *lgiti* is the *pramāṇī*. 5.6.
The other is the *vitāna*. 5.7.
The *anuṣṭubh* [meter] has a *vakā* at the foot. 5.8.
*Sn* does not occur after the first [syllable]. 5.9.
*Aś* occurs after the second and fourth [syllables]. 5.10.
Or otherwise. 5.11.
That which [is derived] from the fourth [syllable]. 5.12.
Pathyā consists of even [pādas] ending in *j*. 5.13.
Viparītaikīya (5.14); Capalā has [the gaṇas] yu and ja in the even [pādas] (5.15);
Vipulā has the seventh [gaṇa] as la in the uneven [pādas] (5.16).
From all [the preceding], it belongs to Saitava. 5.17. And there are two *bhrauṅ* syllables. 5.18.
The *apadacaturūrdhva* consists of an increase of four syllables per quarter-verse. 5.19.
The *āpīḍa* consists of *gāva* [and others]. 5.20. If it begins with *gāva*, it is the *pratyāpīḍa*. 5.21.
And the *pratyāpīḍa* also begins with *gāva* [and others]. 5.22.
In the inversion of the first [meter], there are *mañjarī*, *lavali*, and *amṛtadhārā*. 5.23.
With the structure *udgata* as *ekatasa-jau slau nsau jgau bhnau jlau gsjau sjaug*. 5.24.
The third [meter] is *saurabhaka*, with the structure *naubhgau*. 5.25.
*Lalita* consists of *na*, *sa*, and *u*. 5.26.
*Upasthitapracupita* has the first [pāda] distinct [from the others], consisting of *sa*, *ja*, *bha*, *ga*, *sa*, *ja*, *ra*, *ga*, *na*, *sa*, *na*, *ja*, *ga*, *na*, *sa*, *na*, *ja*, *yu*. 5.27.
*Vardhamāna* has the third [pāda] as *na*, *sa*, *na*, *sa*, *na*, *sa*. 5.28.
Śuddhavirāḍṛṣabha consists of those same [syllables] with *j* and *rā*. (5.29) In the half-verse:
(5.30) Upacitraka consists of *sa*, *so*, *la*, *ga*, *bha*, *au*, *bha*, *gau*. (5.31)
Drutamadhyā consists of *bha*, *bha*, *ga*, *u*, *na*, *ja*, and *jya*.
(5.32) Vegavatī consists of *sa*, *sa*, *ga*, *u*, *bha*, *bha*, *ga*, and *u*. (5.33) Bhadravirāṭ consists of *ta*, *ja*, *u*, *ga*, *ma*, *sa*, *u*, *ga*, and *u*. (5.34)
Ketumatī: sjau-sgaubhraungaug || 5.35 || Ākhyānakī: tau-jgaug-jtau-jgaug || 5.36 || Viparītākhyānakī: jtau-jgaug-tau-jgaug || 5.37 ||

The *hariṇaplutā* consists of the gaṇas sa, sa, la, ga, na, bha, ra, and bha (5.38). The *aparavaktra* consists of the gaṇas na, u, ra, la, ga, na, ja, and ra (5.39). The *puṣpitāgrā* consists of the gaṇas na, u, ya, na, ya, na, ja, ra, and ga (5.40).
*Yavamatī* consists of *r*, *jau*, *jau*, *jrau*, and *g*.
(5.41) *Śikhā* consists of thirty-one [mātrās] at the beginning and thirty-one at the end. (5.42) *Khañjā* occurs when there is a long [syllable] in the odd [pādas]. (5.43)
The pause (*yati*) is a break [in the line]. 6.1.
*Tanumadhyā* consists of *ta*, *na*, *ya*, and *ta*. 6.2.
*Kumāralalitā* consists of *ja*, *sa*, and *ga*. 6.3.

Māṇavakākrīḍitaka consists of the syllables *bha*, *ta*, *la*, and *ga*. (6.4) Citrapadā consists of the syllables *bha*, *na*, *ga*, and *ga*. (6.5) Vidyunmālā consists of the syllables *ma*, *na*, *ga*, and *ga*. (6.6)
The *bhujagaśiśubhṛtā* consists of *na*, *u*, *ma*, and *la*; 6.7. The *halamukhī* consists of *ra*, *na*, and *u*; 6.8.
The *śuddhavirāṭ* consists of *msau*, *j*, and *g*; 6.9.
Paṇava consists of the gaṇas ma, na, ya, and two gurus (mnauygau). 6.10.
Rukmavatī consists of the gaṇas bha, ma, u, and two gurus (bhmausgau). 6.11.
Mayūrasāriṇī consists of the gaṇas ra, ja, u, and two gurus (rjaurgau). 6.12.
Matta consists of ma, bha, sa, and ga. (6.13) Upasthitā consists of ta, ja, and two gas. (6.14) Ekarūpa consists of sa, ja, and two gas. (6.15)

Indravajrā consists of the gaṇas ta, ja, ga, and ga. (6.16) Upendravajrā consists of the gaṇas ja, ta, ja, and ga. (6.17) The Upajātis consist of combinations of these at the beginning and end. (6.18)
Dodhaka consists of the syllables *bha*, *bha*, *ga*, and two *gans*.
(6.19) Śālinī consists of *ma*, *ta*, *u*, *ta*, *ga*, *ga*, and the four *sagas* (the ocean).
(6.20) Vātormī consists of *ma*, *bha*, *u*, *ta*, *ga*, and two *gans*. (6.21)
Bhramaravilasita consists of ma, bha, na, la, u, and ga; 6.22. Rathoddhatā consists of ra, na, u, la, u, and ga; 6.23. Svāgatā consists of sa, ra, na, u, bha, ga, and u; 6.24.
Vṛttā consists of na, nau, and sna; 6.25.
Śyenī consists of rja, u, and laug; 6.26. Jagatī; 6.27.
Vaṃśasthā consists of ja, ta, ja, and ra. (6.28) Indravaṃśā consists of ta, ja, ta, and ra. (6.29) Drutavilambita consists of na, bha, bha, and ra. (6.30)

Toṭaka consists of the syllables *saḥ*. (6.31) Puṭa consists of *na*, *ma*, and *ya*, with eight and four [mātrās] respectively. (6.32) Jaloddhatagati consists of *ja*, *sa*, *ja*, and *sa*, with six and six [mātrās] respectively. (6.33)
Bhujaṅgaprayāta consists of [four] *ya*s. 6.34.
Sragviṇī consists of *ra*s. 6.35. Pramitākṣarā consists of *sa*, *ja*, and two *sa*s. 6.36.
The *vaiśvadevī* consists of *ma*, *u*, *y*, *i*, *ndriya*; the sages [state this].
(6.37) The *navamālinī* consists of *na*, *ja*, *u*, *bhyau*. (6.38) The *praharṣiṇī* consists of *ma*, *na*, *u*, *ja*, *ra*, *au*, with groups of three and ten [syllables]. (7.1)
Rucirā consists of the gaṇas ja, bha, u, ja, u, followed by two navakas (nine mātrās) and a guru.
(7.2) Mattamayūra consists of ma, ta, ya, sa, u, and a guru.
(7.3) Asambādhā consists of ma, ta, na, sa, two gas, and two navakas (nine mātrās), corresponding to the number of sense organs. (7.4)
Aparājitā consists of *na*, *sa*, *la*, *ga*, and *ga*; its meters are *svara* and *ṛṣi*.
(7.5) Praharaṇakalitā consists of *na*, *bha*, *na*, *bha*, *la*, and *ga*.
(7.6) Vasantatilakā consists of *da*, *bha*, *ja*, *ja*, *ga*, and *ga*. (7.7)
The *siṃhonnatā* belongs to Kāśyapa; 7.8. The *uddharṣiṇī* belongs to Saitava; 7.9. The *candrāvartā* belongs to Naunauca; 7.10.
If [the feet] are *māla* and *ṛtunava*, it is [the *mālatī*]. 7.11.
The *maṇiguṇanikara* consists of eight, seven, and six [syllables]. 7.12.
And the *mālinī* consists of *na*, *ma*, *ya*, and *ya*. 7.13.

The *Ṛṣabhagajavilasita* consists of *bha*, *na*, *na*, *ga*, *u*, *ga*, with nine and seven syllables respectively. (7.14) The *Hariṇī* consists of *na*, *sa*, *ma*, *ra*, *u*, *sa*, *la*, *u*, *g*, with six, four, four, and seven syllables respectively. (7.15) The *Pṛthvī* consists of *ja*, *sa*, *ja*, *sa*, *ya*, *la*, *u*, *g*, with eight and nine syllables respectively. (7.16)
Vaṃśapatrapatita consists of *bhr*, *nbh*, *nla*, and *g*; its meters are ten, seven, and six.
(7.17) Mandākrāntā consists of *mbh*, *nt*, *dga*, and *g*; its meters are four, six, and seven.
(7.18) Śikhariṇī consists of *yma*, *bhla*, and *g*; its meters are six, eleven, and seven. (7.19)
*Kusumitalatāvellitā* consists of *ma*, *ta*, *na*, *ya*, *ya*; its meters are five, six, and seven.
(7.20) *Śārdūlavikrīḍita* consists of *ma*, *sa*, *ja*, *sa*, *ta*, *ta*; its meters are twelve, eleven, and seven.
(7.21) *Suvadanā* consists of *ma*, *na*, *bha*, *na*, *ya*, *bha*, *la*, *ga*; its meters are seven, seven, and six. (7.22)
The *gliti* meter (7.23):
*sragdharā* consists of *ma*, *ra*, *bha*, *na*, *ya*, *ya*, with three groups of seven syllables each.
(7.24) *Madraka* consists of *bha*, *ra*, *na*, *ra*, *na*, *ra*, *ga*, *na*, *ra*, *ga*, with ten and twelve syllables [in each quarter]. (7.25)
Aśvalalita consists of the ganas *njau*, *bhjau*, *bhjau*, *bhlau*; [it has] eleven Rudras and twelve Ādityas.
(7.26) Mattākrīḍā consists of the ganas *mautnau*, *naunlaug*; [it has] eight Vasus and fifteen [Ādityas].
(7.27) Tanvī consists of the ganas *bhtaunsau*, *bhaunyau*; [it has] twice twelve Ādityas. (7.28)

*Krauñcapada* consists of *bha*, *ma*, *u*, *bha*, *sa*, *na*, *na*, *u*, *ga*, *bhūta*, *indriya*, and *vasu-ṛṣayaḥ*. (7.29) *Bhujaṅgavijṛmbhita* consists of *ma*, *u*, *ta*, *na*, *u*, *na*, *u*, *rsau*, *la*, *gau*, *vasu*, *rudra*, and *ṛṣayaḥ*. (7.30) *Apavāhaka* consists of *ma*, *na*, *u*, *na*, *u*, *na*, *nsaugau*, *nava-kartu*, and *rasendriyāṇi*. (7.31)
Daṇḍaka is a boat. 7.32.
Caṇḍavṛṣṭiprayāta is the first. 7.33.
Except for Ārāta and Māṇḍavya. 7.34.
The remainder is *pracita*. (7.35) Here, what has not been mentioned is *gāthā*. (8.1) Two *ga* and *la* [constitute a *dvipadā*]. (8.2)
And they are mixed. 8.3. Separately, they are both unmixed and mixed. 8.4.
The Vasus are triads. 8.5.
Half [of the sum] is [the first term]. (8.6) With one added, it is [the second term]. (8.7) The product of the reverse [terms] is twice the first [term], etc. (8.8)
Then one should abandon one [of the two]. (8.9) Twice in the half [verse]. (8.10) Form is empty. (8.11)
Twice in the zero; 8.12. That multiplied by its own half; 8.13.
Twice less two; 8.14.
8.15. [The rule applies] to those ending with that.
8.16. One less than eleven.
8.17. "In the subsequent [cases], it is full; in the subsequent [cases], it is full."
